response.sql: WITH rental_totals AS (SELECT r.rental_id, i.store_id, SUM(p.amount) AS total FROM payment p JOIN rental r ON r.rental_id = p.rental_id JOIN inventory i ON i.inventory_id = r.inventory_id WHERE p.rental_id IS NOT NULL GROUP BY r.rental_id, i.store_id), overall AS (SELECT AVG(total) AS avg_total FROM rental_totals) SELECT rt.store_id, SUM(rt.total) AS combined_total, AVG(rt.total - o.avg_total) AS avg_excess FROM rental_totals rt CROSS JOIN overall o WHERE rt.total > o.avg_total GROUP BY rt.store_id

assumptions.assumption: A rental's payment total is the sum of all its payment amounts. The store comes from rental -> inventory.store_id, and only rentals with at least one payment are included.
'The average rental payment total' is a single average across all paid rentals in every store. Each store's rentals are compared against that one figure.
'How much on average they beat the average by' is the mean of (rental total - average) over the qualifying rentals in each store.

alternatives.interpretation: Each rental is compared with the average rental payment total of its own store, not the overall average.
alternatives.sql: WITH rental_totals AS (SELECT r.rental_id, i.store_id, SUM(p.amount) AS total FROM payment p JOIN rental r ON r.rental_id = p.rental_id JOIN inventory i ON i.inventory_id = r.inventory_id WHERE p.rental_id IS NOT NULL GROUP BY r.rental_id, i.store_id), store_avg AS (SELECT store_id, AVG(total) AS avg_total FROM rental_totals GROUP BY store_id) SELECT rt.store_id, SUM(rt.total) AS combined_total, AVG(rt.total - s.avg_total) AS avg_excess FROM rental_totals rt JOIN store_avg s ON s.store_id = rt.store_id WHERE rt.total > s.avg_total GROUP BY rt.store_id
